threats.threat: A network attacker intercepts admin, browser, or agent traffic
threats.protection: TLS 1.2+, HSTS, a separate mTLS agent listener, and a proxy-only admin listener

evidence.name: serves health over TLS and rejects a plaintext request
should allow the certificate project and reject foreign or deleted projects

threats.threat: Credential stuffing or password guessing against a local account
threats.protection: Argon2id, per-address and per-account limits, lockout, and a generic failure response

evidence.name: should lock the credential for fifteen minutes after five failures and refuse a correct password
should reject the eleventh attempt for one identifier from separate addresses with a rate-limit error

threats.threat: A stolen browser session cookie is replayed
threats.protection: Host-scoped HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookie, CSRF token, rotation, and absolute expiry

evidence.name: should rotate the secret and CSRF token on refresh while keeping the session identity
should set the host-scoped hardened attributes

threats.threat: A cross-site request performs a state change with the user's cookie
threats.protection: Origin and Fetch Metadata checks plus a per-session CSRF header on every unsafe method

evidence.name: should reject an unsafe request that omits the CSRF header even when the session is valid
should add credentials and the CSRF header to unsafe methods

threats.threat: A stolen CLI access or refresh token is replayed
threats.protection: Short-lived JWTs and rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection and family revocation

evidence.name: should revoke the whole family and reject the current refresh token when a rotated token is reused

threats.threat: A principal performs an action outside its role, scope, or project
threats.protection: Deny-by-default RBAC with org, project, and object scopes and capability flags

evidence.name: should deny every action when the principal has no assignment
should never inherit upward from an object assignment

threats.threat: A service identity reaches control-plane actions
threats.protection: A service ceiling in the policy engine rejects control-plane actions even with a forged assignment

evidence.name: should deny control-plane actions to a service principal even with a forged row

threats.threat: A compromised workload reads another project's delivered files
threats.protection: Per-project and per-service host directories, a manifest that cannot change project or root, and a read-only application mount

evidence.name: should reject a mismatched project, service, or output directory
should produce distinct per-service and per-project paths

threats.threat: A stolen agent certificate is used after revocation
threats.protection: Atomic identity revocation, certificate invalidation, listener cache invalidation, and files removed on 401/403

evidence.name: should revoke new, reused, and renewal connections within the process
should clear both local caches after an atomic revoke

threats.threat: A database dump exposes secret or certificate plaintext
threats.protection: AES-256-GCM envelope encryption with a KEK outside the database and per-object AAD

evidence.name: should encrypt and decrypt through the provider
should reject invalid secret envelope lengths and oversized ciphertext

threats.threat: A stolen backup exposes plaintext or is silently corrupted
threats.protection: An age passphrase archive with a checksum manifest and a preflight keyring check

evidence.name: should create a verifiable encrypted archive and reject tampering
should restore into an empty target and verify secrets, audit, CA, and agent certificate

threats.threat: The keyring is read, replaced, or serialized into a log
threats.protection: Absolute path, exact 0600, no symlinks, status-only serialization, and redacted logs

evidence.name: rejects a keyring file that is not exactly 0600
serializes only status fields

threats.threat: An attacker edits, deletes, or truncates the audit chain
threats.protection: Hash chain, HMAC, checkpoints, and verification that reports the first broken event

evidence.name: should detect an edited details value and an edited hash
should detect a deleted tail even when a newer checkpoint exists

threats.threat: A secret, token, CSR, or key is written to a log
threats.protection: Pino path redaction, request URL sanitization, and agent event-only logging

evidence.name: masks the documented top-level, one-level, and request-body paths
should log stable outcomes without tokens, CSRs, or key material

threats.threat: Injection or path traversal reaches SQL, the filesystem, or a route
threats.protection: Parameterized SQL, strict schemas, canonical paths, and malformed-encoding rejection

evidence.name: normalises path variants and rejects malformed encodings
rejects malformed percent encoding at the live listener

threats.threat: An oversized or malformed body exhausts memory or bypasses a limit
threats.protection: Body limits, decoded-value limits, and bounded CSR and certificate envelopes

evidence.name: parses a chunked body once and still applies the secret limit
should reject empty and oversized envelopes before ASN.1 parsing

threats.threat: A flood or repeated request bypasses a rate limit
threats.protection: Per-IP, per-account, per-principal, per-family, and per-route buckets with bounded state

evidence.name: should limit one principal and keep separate buckets
should limit joins per source address

threats.threat: A container escapes its intended privileges or reaches the Docker socket
threats.protection: Non-root users, read-only roots, capability drops, no-new-privileges, resource limits, and no socket mount

evidence.name: validateCompose

evidence.check: Review the host, network, and container checklist before deployment.

threats.threat: A browser secret value leaks into storage, the URL, or the console
threats.protection: Reveal lives only in component state, clears on blur/navigation/timeout, and is never stored

evidence.name: should mask the value and read it only on reveal
should create a secret and clear the value from the dialog

threats.threat: The admin listener is reachable without the proxy or health source guard
threats.protection: Proxy CIDR allowlist, loopback-only health and readiness, and no published admin port

evidence.name: allows health and readiness but not general admin routes
matches IPv4, IPv4-mapped, and IPv6 peers and rejects mixed families

threats.threat: A leaked runtime database credential forges credentials, RBAC, OIDC links, or agent identity
threats.protection: Separate openvault_auth control-plane role; app role loses DML on eight identity tables; production startup assertion

evidence.name: should deny every write on the eight control-plane tables to the app role
should reject the startup assertion when the app connection is over-privileged

threats.threat: Discovery metadata redirects OIDC credentials or tokens to another origin
threats.protection: HTTPS endpoint-origin allowlist and redirect rejection

evidence.name: should reject a cross-origin endpoint for every discovery field
should disable redirects on endpoint requests

threats.threat: An unassigned caller enumerates project or secret names through 403/404 differences
threats.protection: Collection-visibility denials with identical 404 bodies for hidden and missing names

evidence.name: should give an unassigned caller identical 404 bodies for existing and missing secret names
should allow an object-scope reader but hide every other name

threats.threat: `ov doctor` sends the stored bearer to an override origin
threats.protection: Credential-origin binding; TLS and readiness remain unauthenticated on a mismatch

evidence.name: should not send a stored credential to an override origin
should not send a stored credential to an OPENVAULT_URL override

threats.threat: A stolen pruner credential deletes audit evidence with direct SQL
threats.protection: Single-use authorization, definer procedure, completion receipt, and no pruner table authority

evidence.name: should deny direct pruner table authority
should reject a replayed authorization

threats.threat: A secret integrity failure is recorded as a successful read
threats.protection: Allow recorded only after decryption and encoding; every failure writes an error event

evidence.name: should record an integrity error, not an allow, when the newest version is malformed
should write exactly one allow after a successful read

threats.threat: A copied agent join token remains on the clipboard
threats.protection: 30-second best-effort clear with page-level status and manual-clear guidance

evidence.name: should clear a copied join token after the dialog closes
should report a denied clear and keep the manual instruction visible

threats.threat: The data-plane role reads authentication verifiers or identity metadata
threats.protection: Explicit app allowlist, restricted consumer view, and read-only backup role

evidence.name: lets the runtime role read and write data but not run DDL or delete audit events
gives the backup role read-only access to every table

threats.threat: The scaffold endpoint reveals active project names before authorization
threats.protection: Collection-visibility denials with uniform hidden/missing 404 bodies

evidence.name: should hide an existing project from an unassigned caller
should hide a project from an administrator of another project

threats.threat: A stale browser cookie recovers its rotated successor
threats.protection: Pre-rotation CSRF proof on receipt recovery; receipt consumed once

evidence.name: should require the pre-rotation CSRF proof for a late refresh
should require the pre-rotation CSRF proof and serve the successor once
should honor the role matrix and scope eligibility
rejects malformed percent encoding at the live listener
parses a chunked body once and still applies the secret limit
should reject the sixth login from one address within a minute with a rate-limit error
should reject an unsafe request when the Origin does not match the configured origin
should issue a new secret and CSRF token while keeping the public identity and expiry
should allow exactly one of two concurrent refreshes and revoke the family for both tokens
rejects missing and untrusted client certificates and accepts the trusted one
should detect a deleted middle event at the next retained row
masks the documented top-level, one-level, and request-body paths
should produce distinct per-service and per-project paths

should log stable outcomes without tokens, CSRs, or key material
